assessment.nobel_worthiness: Linking population-scale administrative data to the measurement of intergenerational mobility changed what economists and policymakers can observe about opportunity. It combines new data with a framework and designs for neighbourhood causal effects, and it has shaped research, policy and public debate. The case is strong under common criteria of scientific contribution and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: The core mobility and place-based work centres on Chetty, Friedman and Hendren, with Katz central to the Moving to Opportunity line. Limiting the award to three requires leaving out Katz, whose contribution is real but more tied to one experiment and to other work, such as the Autor line. I recognise the case for including Katz.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from roughly 2014 to 2022 and have been widely replicated and extended. Some long-run policy-relevance claims are still being tested, so this is not a case of decades of settled consensus.
uncertainties: Timing: some findings, such as neighbourhood-level causal effects, are still being debated.
How the credit should divide between the data infrastructure and the conceptual or causal contributions.
Whether a younger laureate group is preferred now or later.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the trade-shock evidence together reshaped understanding of labour demand, polarisation and the distributional effects of trade. The contribution combines an explanatory framework with credible empirical identification and has had large policy influence. It is close to the combination of data discovery and a framework that the committee values.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task and the trade-shock literatures. Dorn and Hanson share the China-shock work. Katz is also credited and important to the skills and inequality literature, and other scholars outside this list may belong to the task framework. Choosing three is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work is from the early 2000s and the China-shock papers from 2013 onward. The literature is mature, has been replicated, and has produced follow-ups and debate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to credit the task framework's originators or the trade-shock empirical group.
Ongoing debate over the persistence and interpretation of the trade-shock effects.
Overlap with the mobility candidate through Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work turned adverse-selection theory into measurable, policy-relevant empirical objects: welfare costs of selection, moral hazard and market design in insurance. It offers a clear bridge between theory and data and affects health insurance policy. The conceptual and methodological contribution is distinct and well defined.
assessment.attribution: Einav and Finkelstein are the central empirical-structural pair, often working jointly. Salanie contributes important theory and the earlier empirical test, so omitting him is a closer call. The classic theory credit would sit with earlier laureates.
assessment.maturity: The key contributions span roughly 2010 to 2020 and are well established in academic research and policy use. The field is mature, though the most recent results are still being consolidated.
uncertainties: How far the contribution is distinct from earlier adverse-selection theory that has already been recognised.
Whether Salanie should be included.
Its relative priority against broader, more general discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of fairness, reciprocity and inequity aversion, with experimental evidence, changed how economists treat social preferences in contracts, cooperation and market behaviour. The contribution is both empirical and theoretical, and it has influenced many fields. Behavioural economics has already been recognised, which lowers marginal novelty somewhat.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is central to both the experimental evidence and the theory. Schmidt is co-author of the Fehr-Schmidt model, which is the best-known theoretical formalisation. Falk is an important empirical contributor, and omitting him is a judgment call. Others, such as Bolton and Ockenfels, developed related models, so credit is shared across several groups.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from 1999 and earlier, so the work has had more than twenty-five years of use and replication. Some replication and external-validity debates persist.
uncertainties: External validity of lab-based social-preference measures.
Competing and overlapping models, such as Bolton-Ockenfels, complicate attribution.
Whether the committee sees further behavioural recognition as a priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework underlies modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. Its influence on macroeconomic policy is broad and durable. It is a major synthesis, though several parts of the underlying ideas have earlier recognition.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread widely: Calvo (pricing), Taylor (contracts and the policy rule), Woodford (synthesis), Gali (empirical and theoretical work), and Christiano, Eichenbaum and others (estimated DSGE models). Any three-person subset leaves out clearly deserving contributors, so attribution is the main weakness.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of use. The framework has also been challenged and extended after the global financial crisis and the inflation episode of the 2020s.
uncertainties: Very diffuse credit and overlap with earlier prizes.
Whether the committee would choose the Calvo-Taylor or the Woodford-Gali trio.
Recent critique of the framework's performance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work built a systematic political-economics framework linking electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal outcomes, and it connected theory to cross-country and historical evidence. It is a coherent research programme that opened a field. The empirical identification of some constitutional effects is weaker than in the design-based literatures.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the closest to a joint core, with Besley central to state capacity and accountability. The trio is a natural group but leaves out other founders of political economy, so credit is spread. Political economy more broadly already has some recognition.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work is from the 1990s and 2000s, with extensive follow-up and widespread use in empirical political economy.
uncertainties: Credibility of causal claims in cross-country constitutional comparisons.
Overlap with Acemoglu-Johnson-Robinson recognition on institutions.
Division of credit across the broader political-economics field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint mechanism of Kiyotaki and Moore, together with the financial accelerator literature, explains how credit frictions amplify and propagate shocks, and it became central after the global financial crisis. It is a conceptual contribution with clear policy relevance. Some empirical identification of the mechanisms is indirect.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clear originators of the credit-cycle mechanism. Gertler is central to the financial accelerator and to the policy applications, partly with Bernanke, who has already been recognised and is not listed here. Gilchrist is an empirical contributor. The group could be framed in several ways.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers are from 1997 or earlier, and the literature was extended and tested after 2008. It is a mature, widely adopted framework.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Bernanke recognition for the financial accelerator, and with Gertler's presence in the New Keynesian candidate.
Whether the committee judges the macro-finance work to be mainly theory with indirect validation.
Diffusion of credit across several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how researchers reason about what data can reveal under weak assumptions, and it influenced empirical practice by making assumptions explicit. It is a deep methodological contribution, though use in applied work is narrower than design-based or regression methods. It is a plausible econometric recognition.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear founder of the approach. Tamer and Molinari were central in developing inference and moment-inequality methods, so credit is relatively traceable to this group. Other contributors, such as Chernozhukov, Hong, Tamer and Imbens, partly overlap.
assessment.maturity: Manski's foundational work dates from the late 1980s and 1990s, and the inference theory from the 2000s onward. The methodology is established, though applied adoption remains selective.
uncertainties: Breadth of applied impact relative to other candidates.
Whether the committee would credit the founder alone or also the later inference developers.
Overlap with other econometrics candidates.
